A1.justification: Both complete 21-page PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original orbital simulations, lattice and Othello experiments, transfer evaluations, and LLM force-prediction experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised orbital inductive-bias plots.

M1.justification: The synthetic-task adaptation procedure, extrapolative-predictability calculations, oracle comparisons, and model architectures remain unchanged. The revised plots do not establish an algorithm or training-method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same orbital and two-body scenarios, lattice problems with two to five states, Othello tasks, and LLM force prediction. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same trained and untrained sequence models, linear/MLP and nearest-neighbor oracles, trajectory baselines, and three LLMs. The newly cited related work is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The stated sampling procedures, splits, training budgets, metrics, and adaptation settings remain unchanged, including Appendix B.1's modified experiment. The absolute-value caption clarification does not establish a protocol change or an experimental rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 revises Figure 7's evidence for the existing robustness test using two-body systems and partially observed trajectories. Its poor-alignment conclusion remains; the Othello ablations and other supplementary analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: The tables retain identical uncertainty displays. Symbolic-regression restart counts and the significance statement for next-token partitions are also unchanged, with no added seed information or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 4 and 7 contain revised plotted values and point patterns. Figure 7's oracle values now extend to approximately 2 rather than 5. These localized revisions retain the poor-alignment finding; all nine tables contain unchanged results.

T1.justification: The world-model definitions, Equations 1–8, oracle construction, and next-token partition mathematics remain unchanged. The absolute-value plotting clarification does not revise the formal definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: inductive-bias probes assess world models, and strong sequence prediction can coexist with weak world-model alignment and task-specific heuristics.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the interpretations involving piecemeal physical laws and next-token state partitions, along with the limitation that analysts must specify a candidate world model. The revised plots introduce no new interpretation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: The captions of Figures 4 and 7 newly disclose that plotted quantities are absolute values of the inductive-bias metric. This adds a limited technical reporting detail; implementation settings, prompts, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Lee, Rush, and Vafa (2025), contrasting its DFA-complexity and computation questions with this paper's empirical probe. The expanded Bricken et al. reference identifies an already cited work, rather than adding another research direction.

P1.justification: v4 revises a related-work paragraph, changes several appendix cross-reference labels, corrects bibliographic presentation, and makes small punctuation edits. The main narrative and section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 7 are redrawn with square plotting panels, revised axes, and expanded captions. Figure 5 moves from page 8 to page 7, while caption typography and float placement change elsewhere without adding or removing displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, v4 makes the calibration plots clearer through square panels and explicit absolute-value captions, and sharpens the related-work comparison. These are limited quality gains. The reasons for the revised plotted values are not documented, so those revisions do not establish improved experimental validity.
